chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi' asked Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him):

About a young girl whom her father marries off, then he dies while she is still small, then she grows up before her husband enters into her (consummates the marriage). Is the marriage valid for her, or is the matter in her hands? He said: 'The marriage performed by her father is valid for her.'

key_terms.الْأَمْرُ إِلَيْهَا: The matter is in her hands (her choice)
key_terms.يَدْخُلَ بِهَا: He enters into her (consummates the marriage)
key_terms.يُزَوِّجُهَا: He marries her off (arranges her marriage)

ai.seo_question: Does a father's marriage of his minor daughter remain binding if he dies before consummation?
ai.summary: Imam Ar-Ridha (as) establishes that the father's right of *kafā'ah* (guardianship) remains binding even after the daughter reaches maturity, provided consummation has not yet occurred. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view that the initial contract initiated by the guardian retains its validity without requiring a new consent phase upon her majority, distinguishing it from schools where the choice (*ikhtiyār*) reverts fully to the woman. This principle underscores the continuity of the father's authority in the formation of the marital bond until physical union is realized.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.4391 - Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi' asked Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha (as) about a young girl who was married off by her father, and then the father died while she was still a child.
When she grew older, before her husband consummated the marriage, does the marriage remain valid, or is the matter in her hands?
Imam (as) replied: "The marriage performed by her father is valid for her."
